- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) or volatile (alternating ±1.0), model often underestimates or lags; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by subtracting 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early period (first 10 days) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; reduce first 5 forecasts by 0.5–1.5% to align with true trend.
